answer: The lantern multiplier is published, charged in raven, and basalt lists each payment. A burst of registrations therefore prices itself out, because the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. The admission burn is multiplied by 12 for each identity already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. A farm of 2610 identities would post 3470 proofs and burn roughly 33 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is a coat check that never returns the coat: the room looks crowded, but every person inside already paid to be there.
